Commentary.Commentary: Right then, the washout in this game means that Bangladesh cannot lose this series and will have another chance to seal it in the third match while the Kiwis will hope they can at least finish on level terms. The 3rd T20I will be played on 31st December, Sunday at 5.30 am IST (12 am GMT), but as you know, you can join us early for all the build-up. Until then, cheers and goodbye!

Bad news folks! The inevitable has happened as the umpires have decided to call this game off due to the persistent rain. Even though, New Zealand ​​​​​Finn Allen early again, they got off to a flashy start with Tim Seifert smashing a quick-fire 43 off just 23 balls while the other batters struggled. Daryl Mitchell was not timing the ball at all and got lucky on a couple of occasions and Glenn Phillips looked unsettled as well. Bangladesh recovered well after the Powerplay through their spinners, who bowled economically. However, Shoriful Islam was once again excellent and provided them with an early breakthrough and Tanzim Hasan Sakib also got one, but they were pretty ordinary in the field and dropped a few good chances and they will need to be much better in the next game. We could get only 10 overs in this game where New Zealand were at 72/2, and unfortunately, the rain gods showed no mercy and we could not get any further action.

UPDATE - 2 pm IST (8.30 am GMT) - No good news yet again. The time is running out and the forecast isn't very promising. According to the calculations, if at all the match starts, Bangladesh will have to chase down 46 in 5 overs and 85 in 10 overs, whatever is possible with the time left in hand. The fourth official is out on the field with an Umbrella. We might hear something soon.

UPDATE - 1.20 pm IST (7.50 am GMT) - The rain is still strong and the covers are intact. The most expected start can be a 5-over run chase but other than that, it looks done for the day. The latest the game can start is 2.58 pm IST (9.28 am GMT).

UPDATE - 1 pm IST (7.30 am GMT) - The rain has not stopped and the covers are still on as we all play the waiting game. In other new news, Australia have won the Boxing Day Test against Pakistan in fine fashion.

Oh..no! The rain has got pretty heavy now and the umpires have finally decided to call for the covers. The players are going off and this break could help the Kiwis as their batters were really struggling out there. Stick with us for further updates.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin! The players are already out in the middle and a bit of a light and firework show is going on around the ground. Finn Allen and Tim Seifert are the two openers for New Zealand. Bangladesh going with spin straightaway as Mahedi Hasan has the new ball in hand. Let's play...
New Zealand (Unchanged Playing XI) - Finn Allen, Tim Seifert (WK), Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Mark Chapman, James Neesham, Mitchell Santner (C), Adam Milne, Tim Southee, Ish Sodhi, Ben Sears.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Soumya Sarkar, Rony Talukdar (WK), Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Shamim Hossain (In place of Litton Das), Towhid Hridoy, Afif Hossain, Mahedi Hasan, Mustafizur Rahman, Shoriful Islam, Rishad Hossain, Tanzim Hasan Sakib.
TOSS - Bangladesh have won the toss and elected to BOWL first.

On the other hand, it's high time for the Kiwis to change the strategy they took in the first match and get control of the series. The Kiwis were struggling to have a substantial partnership, and the top order failed to trigger the head start as three batters of the Black Caps got dismissed in the first eight balls of their innings. However James Neesham in the middle-order held the loose strings of his team and scored 48 runs. The bowlers tried to put up a good show by attacking the batters but the required run rate was too low and Adam Milne and Ish Sodhi's overs were way too much expensive for the given target. The Men in Black needs to come up with some exceptional strategies to get today's match in their pocket. The batters need to put some confidence on the pitch and play the match like a host team. Will the Kiwis come back in the series? Let's find out! Toss and team updates to follow.

Bangladesh are clearly on a history-creating spree in New Zealand. First, the historic win in the third ODI, and now they have the first-ever T20 win against New Zealand in New Zealand. Special credit to the bowling unit as they executed their plans immaculately after being asked to bowl first Shoriful Islam emerged as a standout performer claiming 3 wickets in which the first two came in his first over. Mahedi Hasan and Mustafizur Rahman also contributed with wickets each. The T20 debutante Tanzim Hasan Sakib made the match memorable for him as he secured his maiden wicket. In the chase, it was not much of a problem for the Bengla Tigers to match up with the target as Liton Das made it clear for his team to stay not out from the start till the end scoring 42 runs. The team will be looking to continue the same commitment in this match as they really want to continue this dominating performance to take the series home and keep the pressure on the Kiwis.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the 2nd T20 in the Bangladesh tour of New Zealand. The hosts, New Zealand will take on the visiting Bangladesh side for the second time in this T20 series at the Bay Oval Stadium, Mount Maunganui.
... MATCH DAY ...

After making history in the ODI series, Bangladesh have swiftly taken the lead in the shortest format with an impressive performance. They clinched their first-ever ODI victory against the Kiwis in New Zealand in the previous game and carried that winning momentum forward. Once again, their bowlers played a pivotal role in securing the win. The pace trio of Mustafizur Rahman, Shoriful Islam, and Tanzim Hasan Sakib displayed brilliance and will likely be instrumental in the upcoming match. Mahedi Hasan's precision was commendable, and should they seek more spin options, Mehidy Hasan could be introduced. Additionally, their newest member, Rishad Hossain, has shown promise with the ball and can also be a useful batter. With experienced batters like Litton Das, Najmul Hossain Shanto, and Soumya Sarkar, the onus will be on them to amass runs, while the likes of Towhid Hridoy and Afif Hossain provide strength in the lower order, solidifying Bangladesh's lineup. Meanwhile, New Zealand, eager to bounce back after a few setbacks, will look to their explosive openers Finn Allen and Tim Seifert for a strong start. Daryl Mitchell, fresh from a significant Indian T20 League contract, and the attacking Glenn Phillips need to capitalize on their experience. While Rachin Ravindra could be an option, the presence of James Neesham and Mitchell Santner further bolsters their middle order. Tim Southee spearheads the pace with Ben Sears and Adam Milne, and the inclusion of Jacob Duffy could add more depth. Ish Sodhi's prowess in this format is noteworthy, and Santner's all-round abilities can be game-changing. Both teams are poised for a fierce contest, with the BlackCaps aiming to level the series and the Bangla Tigers keen to seal it. The outcome promises to be captivating.
